mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 5.0% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.0% and remains >5.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 140,000 new jobs monthly for two months predicts stronger consumer demand and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 140,000 and remains >140,000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or non-significant (p > 0.05) despite the labor signal, or PAYEMS does not exceed 140,000 for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the HOUST index (units) of 2% or more over the prior month indicates weakening demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decreases by at least 2% in the previous month relative to the month before
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or statistically insignificant (p > 0.05), or HOUST decline is less than 2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 102.5) suggests supply-side constraints, which tends to produce positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days when combined with a rising UNRATE.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 102.5 and UNRATE rises over the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or not significant (p > 0.05) despite the combined signal, or INDPRO does not fall below 102.5.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 3% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver negative 20-day forward returns as investors anticipate rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains >3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or not significantly different from zero (p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL never exceeds 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 5.0% combined with a 10% one-month increase in GDPC1 (GDP) suggests labor market softening and economic momentum favoring positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% and GDPC1 increases by >10% in the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not significant (p > 0.05), or either proxy fails to meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in RSAFS of at least 5% indicates financial market stress, which typically precedes negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns in contractionary regimes.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by at least 5% in the current month relative to the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive or not significant (p > 0.05), or RSAFS decline is less than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), the S&P 500 is expected to post positive 60-day forward returns as lower discounting amplifies future earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: regime: FEDFUNDS < 1.0% for at least 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative or not significant (p > 0.05) despite the easing, or FEDFUNDS does not remain below 1.0% for 4 months.
